svg.title: Spinal cord or root: upper motor neuron signs below a sensory level mean the cord, and which modalities are lost sorts anterior, posterior, central and Brown-Sequard cord syndromes; a lower motor neuron pattern means the roots, either cauda equina (an emergency) or a single radiculopathy; each column gives the presentation and the causes

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Cord or root? Motor exam + the LOWEST sensory level

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: upper motor neuron (UMN), brain or cord: subtle bulk loss, tone ↑, hyperreflexia, upgoing toe

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: lower motor neuron (LMN), root or nerve: wasting, tone ↓, reflexes ↓ or absent

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: NO motor or sensory function below the level, incl. rectal tone + perianal sensation = COMPLETE

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: cervical → arms + legs · thoracic → both legs ± bowel, bladder

svg.text: incomplete: WHICH modalities are lost names the syndrome

svg.text: cervical → one arm · lumbar → one leg
